questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I’ve travelled around Australia before and wanted to experience what it’s like to actually live there, build an everyday life abroad, and embrace everything that comes with it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy as long as you took the time to read the emails carefully. They explained everything well, and I didn’t really experience any problems.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction day and a virtual orientation meeting, both of which I would recommend attending. In these meetings I met the contact person at my host university, who explained everything I needed to know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I knew a Danish acquaintance who was already living in a large house owned by a landlord who rented out rooms to exchange students, so finding accommodation was quite easy for me. However, I know that it can be difficult, although people managed to find a place in the end. Many landlords in Sydney prefer you to be there in person, so quite a few people only found accommodation after they arrived. Personally, I would recommend finding housing in Sydney and NOT living in Parramatta (I was at the Parramatta campus), where WSU is located.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It worked great for me! Would highly recommend living with other people since there weren’t many opportunities to socialize and get to know each other at the university. I definitely spent most of my time with the other exchange students in my house.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Don't expect to live in luxury. Sydney is expensive, however I've heard that on campus is not that great compared to how expensive it is. I lived off campus for 5600 kr./month for a room, which is a really great price in Sydney - but the house weren't the prettiest :)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy when you read the mails carefully - they explain everything. If I had any questions, my contact person was relatively quick to respond on my enquiries. I didn't have any problems with getting the subjects I wanted either, so I can't really complain about the registration process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could submit an official enquiry, and your contact person would help answering your questions. You could also, if needed, request a video call.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Had no problems. Got the subjects I wanted - had two conflicting subjects, but it was easy for me to just change one of the subjects to another one so I was able to attend all my classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Attend online meetings and read the mails carefully and multiple times.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some were really good, others not so much. Academically much different from KU.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: If you are a Political Science student at KU, then it will be no problem getting through the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much smaller classes - some more interactive than others, but definitely less demanding in terms of both preparation for classes and the level of the classes. Not much group work, more just casual talk with the teachers.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Political Economy of Development (HUMN7031)
Fundamentals of Cyber Crime and Security in a Global World (CULT5002)
Borders, Mobilities and Justice (HUMN5001)
Perspectives in Criminology (CULT3018) - Online Class

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really liked the subject and my professor in Borders, Mobilities and Justice (HUMN5001). It was the class reminding me most of subjects I've liked at KU (i.e. Politisk Teori). The class Political Economy of Development was also fine! The two best subjects I had. 

If you want more flexibility I would also recommend choosing one online class (it is permitted to take 25% of your classes online, which in my case was one course). The class Perspectives in Criminology was okay, but not my favourite and very far from Political Science as was Fundamentals of Cyber Crime and Security in a Global World.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything is just quite expensive. I travelled a lot - would highly recommend, but of course very costly.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries and domestic flights were more expensive than expected. However my rent was less expensive than what I would expect in Sydney, but I know I was quite lucky in terms of my rent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't join any, but I got mails about clubs you could join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Didn't pay attention to it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore the different areas in Sydney. Go to Blue Mountains. Travel if possible around Australia - so much to see!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Try and have a balance between traveling i.e. take a weekend to Melbourne or Blue Mountains, and get to know your favorite areas in Sydney. Enjoy that Sydney has everything from a bustling CBD to amazing beaches. Rent a car and go north or south of Sydney.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I went with a close friend which definitely made adjusting easier. However, Sydney and Australia is pretty "European" in terms of culture (also with influence from Asia). Even though you are far away it is not that big of a culture shock.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Didn't really find it challenging. It was very easy to adapt and Australiens are very kind and openminded.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A lot of people live a very balanced and active lifestyle. Loved running in Centennial Park or along the coast! They have a lot of yummy asian foods as well, I'll definitely miss the Sushi Rolls :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Read. The. Mails. And carefully - they send you one especially important mail with everything you need to do and know! Read it multiple times and use it as a check list. 2) The campuses are pretty spread out in the suburbs of Sydney. I was in Parramatta - very easy to get to with train from Sydney, but would everyday chose to have more transport time (was only on campus 1-2 times a week) rather than living in the suburbs !! 3) Don't stress about the academic level.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't have exams. I just had to do three assignments in each subject along the semester. The three assignments in each subject would then result in a grade.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was just amazing. Loved it so much! Met so many amazing people and got so many amazing new memories. Loved the city and Australia as a whole.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The difference in timezones between DK and AU. A blessing and a curse.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
